exposure: fire-specific particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter <=2.5 mum (PM2.5)
cohort: The study included 1788 children born in the Latrobe Valley, Australia, who were under two years old during the Hazelwood mine fire (Feb-March 2014).
finding: Children with medium or high exposure to fire-specific PM2.5 during infancy had higher rates of overall emergency department presentations over a five-year period compared to those with low exposure.
